newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 1996 public debt at 51.2 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Polish 1996 public debt at 51.2 pct of GDP.

text.p: Poland's public debt rose 10.9 percent in 1996 to 185.39 billion zlotys and is seen at 218 billion at the end of 1997, the head of the finance ministry's public debt department, said on Wednesday.
Piotr Dziewulski told a news conference the share of public debt in the gross domestic product (GDP) fell to 51.2 percent in 1996 from 58.5 percent in 1995.

"1996 was another year of falling debt in relation to GDP," Dziewulski said. He said domestic debt amounted to 79.4 billion zlotys, or 57.2 percent of the total, and foreign debt was 106.0 billion zlotys, or 42.8 percent.
The ministry said that 93.3 percent of the total domestic debt was in the form of government securities.

He said the government would limit financing of the budget deficit in the National Bank of Poland in 1997 and wanted to end up with zero balance at the end of the year even though the limit of borrowing in the NBP this year was two percent of budget spending plan, or 2.55 billion zlotys.
"This limit will be used only in the case of extraordinary problems with getting financing elsewhere," Dziewulski said.
